study.question: Does a second temporal moment within action-by-match cells add validation utility beyond counts, mean one-day freshness, the existing bucketed history pools, and an equal-capacity deterministic squared-mean replacement? Does the evidence partition alter that effect?
study.hypothesis: Observation: g0-r0011-exclusive_freshness AUC 0.6202566053518737 exceeds exclusive_presence 0.6195023078260058; cumulative_freshness 0.6200470321474675 exceeds cumulative_presence 0.6196752395004308. These single-seed differences are preliminary. Latest candidate-supplied first-512 diagnostics show 3.9414 occupied exclusive cells/impression and 0.19055 of all 16 cells have more than one event, establishing some opportunity but not predictive value for a distributional summary. Source inspection shows that the correction retains only count and mean d=exp(-age/86400) per cell, while the backbone retains pooled log2 age buckets. This loses within-cell decay dispersion. For identical action/category/brand, decays [0.55,0.65] and [0.6,0.6] give the same count=2, mean=0.6 and recency buckets [16,16], yet E[d^2]=0.3625 versus 0.36. This is an algebraic collision, not observed predictive evidence. Hypothesis: exposing E[d^2], jointly with mean d, permits useful within-cell temporal distinctions beyond extra capacity or a nonlinear mean feature. It is also a half-day mean decay, so any gain does not uniquely establish a dispersion rather than timescale explanation.

nearest_work.difference: Retains every inherited module and initialization as a prefix. Adds one zero-initialized 16->32 bias-free projection for temporal second moments before the same residual ReLU. Changes the information in the new feature path, not retrieval or training. Existing single-mean source is the performance anchor, not a capacity-matched causal control.

Crosses cumulative versus exclusive evidence with true second moment versus squared mean, testing whether the previous basis-by-freshness interaction extends to second-order evidence. Raw count/first/second sums transform linearly between the two bases; basis choice is a reparameterization.

DIN uses target-conditioned local activation and unnormalized weighted sum pooling to preserve interest intensity. This study uses fixed field-match pools and explicit fixed-scale decay moments. baseline_reference.py uses softmax-normalized attention and is only a field-adapted reference; it is not an exact DIN replication. DIN inspection does not establish priority for moment summaries.

study.proposed_difference: Append 16 true second moments E[d^2] or 16 deterministic squared means E[d]^2 to the unchanged 32 count/mean features, using an appended 16->32 projection summed into the existing first correction preactivation. Initialize the appended weight to zero; preserve the initial ancestor function and seeded inherited tensors. Every cell adds exactly 512 parameters: predicted total 17,140,675, dense 61,987, subject to host verification. Cross this replacement with exclusive/cumulative evidence (four equal-capacity cells). Both selected features are zero for empty cells, in [0,1], and coincide for singleton and constant-age cells. Their difference is variance in decay space. This candidate distinguishes some histories collapsed by the ancestor, without representing event order or detecting bursts in general. Both E[d^2] and E[d]^2 and all bases are computed in all variants; equal source arithmetic does not establish equal measured cost.
predictions: Primary predeclared contrasts: exclusive_second AUC minus exclusive_square AUC; cumulative_second minus cumulative_square. Mechanism support requires beating the matching squared-mean control, not only the lower-capacity ancestor. Treat either seed-42 result as preliminary; predeclare delta >=0.0002 as a practical follow-up trigger, not a significance threshold. Selection stays validation-only.

Predict that exclusive_second will beat exclusive_square and g0-r0011-exclusive_freshness; the cumulative pair is a replication of the information contrast under a different basis, not an independent sample. Compute the difference of those two contrasts to describe basis interaction, without assuming its sign.

Host should verify identical parameter counts, finite logits and gradients, padding/order invariance within 1e-4, exact masked empty-path zero, zero-length equivalence within 1e-4, singleton E[d^2]=E[d]^2 within 1e-5, 0<=mean^2<=second<=mean<=1 up to 1e-5, and count/basis identities within 1e-4. Missing/nonfinite or failed checks invalidate that execution, not the scientific hypothesis.

First-512 label-free diagnostics should show nonzero within-cell variance for at least some multi-event cells; measure active projection weights and trained-head replacement effect. These checks show opportunity and activation only, not predictive attribution or population prevalence.

Report full-population validation ROC-AUC, unweighted Logloss, sample counts, train/wall/allocated GPU seconds when supplied, throughput, whole-batch p50/p95 and peak memory. An AUC gain with Logloss worsening by more than 0.00002 or measured wall/latency rising by more than 10% is an explicit quality-cost tradeoff requiring review before claiming practical improvement. Do not claim equal-compute superiority from a matched-epoch suite.

Use only frozen host slices (history length, hour, behavior composition, frequency and supplied missing/unseen slices) with sample/positive/negative counts. Slice analyses and first-512 variance summaries remain exploratory; no new scored slices or label access are introduced.
falsifiers: If both true-moment cells fail to beat their squared-mean replacements, incremental predictive utility of this implementation is unsupported. If squared-mean controls explain the gain over ancestors, attribute it to capacity/representation/optimization rather than added temporal information.
If only one partition benefits, restrict conclusions to that representation and investigate the interaction; a single best arm cannot establish a general temporal mechanism.

If variance is essentially zero or the new projection/readout never becomes active, the implementation offers an inadequate mechanism test. Investigate a discriminating follow-up within reserve instead of calling the temporal-information hypothesis refuted.

If a favorable seed-42 contrast disappears or reverses on frozen paired seeds 43 and 44, retain the first observation and report seed sensitivity; no repeated support. If the candidate fails to exceed the stronger frozen source, no new best supported model is established.
alternative_explanations: An added linear path may improve optimization or nonlinear representation even with redundant inputs; squared-mean controls have identical capacity and initialization, but do not perfectly match all feature distributions or effective information rank.

E[d^2] is E[exp(-age/43200)] as well as a second moment: this suite cannot uniquely separate a half-day timescale explanation from within-cell dispersion. A future scale-versus-distribution replacement would be required.

Single-seed selection noise, accumulated validation search and checkpoint selection can explain small differences; paired seeds reduce seed uncertainty but do not provide a fresh holdout or erase search bias.

History truncation (85.16% at 128 events in a candidate-supplied 512-impression snapshot) can distort temporal summaries; no events beyond the frozen causal prefix are authorized. Publisher static snapshot dates remain undocumented, limiting production point-in-time interpretation.
Exclusive and cumulative normalized bases expose different optimization geometry, despite invertible raw moments. Their factorial interaction is not proof of extra available information.
First-512 diagnostics are candidate supplied, potentially unrepresentative and only label-free; nonzero counterfactual head effects are not evidence of improved predictions.
